notes: Hand-designed slice arena. Player at the bottom, Brown+Grey+Teal across the top.
The centre pillar sits on the Teal->player line, so Teal must bank a ricochet off a side wall.
The east pillar is the bank-shot reflector: a shell from Teal can clear the centre pillar by going around it, bank off the east pillar's west face, and reach the player beyond.

Cover depth: the centre pillar's lower tier. With the upper tier alone, Brown's and Grey's lines to the player spawn were exactly tangent to its corners -- a knife edge where a 0.1-unit nudge gave one of them a clear 10-unit lane. The lower tier turns that graze into a real chord.

claims.why: The row-5 cell exists for exactly this: with the row-4 block alone, Brown's and Grey's lines to the player spawn were tangent to its corners, and a 0.1-unit nudge opened a clear lane. spawnBlockRobust checks both intact and breached walls; measured to hold under both with the row-5 cell in place.

notes: Reshaped in the 2026-07-31 balance pass: the bar is a FULL destructible barrier with three solid anchors, so the halves START sealed -- tanks cannot cross and shells cannot pass until someone blasts a hole. Breaching the bar IS the level.

claims.why: Blowing the bar's inner end opens the UPPER pair's lane -- the trade the level is built around. Fails if a solid outer end went missing or the trade stopped existing.
The mirrored upper lane.
The LOWER pair stays shielded by the bar's solid anchors however much is destroyed.
Mirrored lower lane.

notes: The rocket debut: two Olives (DEFENSIVE_ROCKET, one rocket in flight) flank high behind destructible shields, with a brown-grey-brown trio behind solid cover.

Each flank column (4 and 28) is open floor top-to-bottom EXCEPT the olive's shield, so blasting a shield opens that vertical lane end-to-end, both ways. The shield is the level's trade, one per flank.

The north anchors deny the olives any diagonal into the player half. The browns' spawn lines are shut by a REAL CHORD through the centre pillar -- the pillar's lower tier exists for ARENA_01's reason: with its upper tier alone, a breached centre peek left both brown lines blocked only by a corner tangency.
The centre peek 'x' (rows 18-20) is breachable mid-field cover on the centre axis, not a spawn-line blocker.

claims.why: The olive's shield is the ONLY wall on its flank column: breaching opens the lane end-to-end both ways -- the player can hunt up it, the olive's rockets command it down.
The mirrored flank: one shield per side is the level's trade.
Unlike level 2, breaching opens NO spawn-to-spawn line here: the trade is lanes for mobile tanks, not spawn lines.
Mirrored olive: same rule.
Trio brown: the centre pillar keeps its line shut after the peek is breached.
Trio grey: same pillar.
Trio brown, mirrored.

The row-5 chord-maker exists for this: with row 4 alone, both browns' post-breach blocks were a single-point corner tangency that a 0.1-unit player nudge opened into a full lane. Found by slab math in review. spawnBlockRobust checks both intact and breached walls; measured to hold under both with the chord-maker in place.

notes: The crossfire debut, and the FIRST shipped board that is not 33x27: 45x33, so the extra space is what makes two simultaneous fronts readable instead of merely crowded.

Six enemies in two fronts at ninety degrees to each other. NORTH is the suppressing front -- GREEN, grey, brown across row 4, behind the bar. EAST is the mobile front -- teal, olive, teal down column 40, inside the player's own half, behind the solid east wall.

The green at (10, 4) is the RICOCHET_SNIPER debut, and it is here because it answers the board's own weakness. 35 of the 151 open cells are seen by no enemy from its spawn -- one broad region, NOT a tidy corner. Green's ricochets reach 29 cells it has no direct line to, and 20 of those are cells no enemy can otherwise see at all: it covers 20 of the 35. It is stationary like a brown, so the north front keeps its character; it simply does not accept the bar as cover. Column 10 and not 13: from column 13 its reach was larger (44 cells) but it could ricochet onto the nudged player spawn once the bar was breached, which this arena's spawnBlockRobust claim forbids. Both figures are recomputed by arena-validation.test.ts.

The two fronts want opposite cover, and that IS the level. Cell (22, 22) sits in the bar's shadow -- shut to the north, wide open to the teal at (40, 13) shooting along the corridor below the bar. Cell (28, 22), six cells east, is the exact inverse: shut to every east tank by the east wall, open to the grey down the bar's gap at column 25. Breaking one front's line steps you into the other's. Four lane claims pin both cells in both wall phases.

The two walls are deliberately different KINDS of problem. The bar is porous, solid only in alternating segments, and breachable at columns 13 and 31; the east wall is solid throughout except for one corridor gap, and must be FLANKED rather than blown. From the player's half that means the corridor above it or the open rows below its south end; it is open north of the bar too, but that is out of the play area. Level 2 taught breaching; level 4 says not every wall answers to it.

Blowing the bar at column 31 opens that column top-to-bottom, giving the brown at (31, 4) a line down to row 28 -- alongside the player spawn, never onto it: the spawn's own blockers are the bar's solid anchors, which no breach touches. That is why spawnBlockRobust holds here and all six sightlineAfterBreach claims read false, unlike level 2 where breaching is meant to open spawn lines.
The destructible at (19, 19) is mid-field cover for the player's left-hand approach, not a spawn-line blocker: losing it hands the teal at (40, 13) a line onto (16, 22).

Measured against the shipped levels on the same probe -- open cells (destructibles EXCLUDED, they are walls until destroyed) seen by no enemy from its spawn, walls intact: arena-04 is 35 of 151 = 23.2%, the tightest of the four, against arena-01 35/86 = 40.7%, arena-02 41/83 = 49.4%, arena-03 30/88 = 34.1%. The intended step up in pressure for the last level. These five numbers are recomputed by arena-validation.test.ts rather than left as unpinned prose.

claims.why: North-west GREEN, the ricochet sniper: the bar's solid cell at column 3 stands on its direct line and no breach touches it. Its BANK paths are checked separately and in two places -- structuralFailures forbids a stationary banker any ricochet onto the spawn with walls intact, and this arena's spawnBlockRobust claim extends that to the breached phase under nudges. Column 3 is where green survives BOTH; column 4 did not.
North-centre grey: blocked by the bar's solid cell at column 7, straight up the player's own column.

North-east brown: blocked by the bar's solid cell at column 9. Breaching column 10 opens the column beside the player, not the spawn itself -- the lane claim below is the other half of that statement.
East teal, high: the column-11 wall at row 6 is solid and stays so.
East olive: the column-11 wall at row 7. The rocket never gets a free line on a respawning player, which with six enemies on the board it must not.
East teal, low: the column-11 wall at row 8.

All six spawn blocks are solid bar cells or solid column-11 cells, so unlike level 2 the spawn survives a full breach. Measured 0 of 24 nudge probes open in BOTH wall phases; the claim is what keeps a future edit from turning one of those six blockers destructible without noticing.
CROSSFIRE, half one of four: the north's centre gun cannot touch (7, 7) in either phase -- the row-4 bar shadows it.

CROSSFIRE: but the east teal owns that same cell along the row-5 corridor. Cover from the north is exposure to the east. Together with the pair below, this is the level's whole idea, stated so an edit cannot quietly undo it.

CROSSFIRE, the inversion: two cells east, the grey's line is open down COLUMN 8's gap in the bar -- not column 7, which is one of the three solid cells holding the grey off the player spawn. Widening column 7 would open that spawn line; column 8 is already open floor.
CROSSFIRE: and the east teal is shut out by the column-11 wall. (7, 7) and (9, 7) are exact opposites, and stay so through a full breach.

The bar's west breach: column 4 is otherwise clear from row 1 to row 7, so blowing that cell opens a north-south lane into the player's half. NOTE both endpoints are plain floor -- green sits at column 3, not 4 -- so unlike this arena's other lanes nothing pins this one to a live spawn. It measures the destructible at (4, 4), which is the thing worth measuring.
The bar's east breach, and the bigger trade: column 10 is clear top to bottom, so this one opens the full height of the board -- down to row 9, level with the player spawn but not onto it.
Losing the mid-field cover at (6, 6) hands the east teal the player's left-hand approach. The cover is the player's, so this is a cost the PLAYER pays for a stray shot, not a trade they choose.
